cheat_sheet.title: Python Data and Mathematical Foundations — Structural Cheat Sheet
cheat_sheet.introduction: This sheet turns Python Data and Mathematical Foundations into visible relationships. It is a reference for planning, tracing, debugging, and explaining—not a list to memorize.
cheat_sheet.why_it_matters: The level contributes directly to a responsible machine-learning model card and prototype. Each concept helps the learner move from an ambiguous task to a contract, a representation, a verified transition, and an explainable result.

mental_model.summary: Represent the work as vectors, matrices, distributions, functions, losses, and error costs before translating it into implementation details.
reasoning_cycle: Model variables, state, constraints, and relationships

output_questions: What shape and state are promised?

common_mistakes: Starting with syntax before defining the input-output contract.
Combining current state and a candidate update so rejection cannot be safe.
Treating an observed normal result as proof for every boundary.
Choosing a structure because it is familiar rather than because its operations match the constraints.
Ignoring empty, missing, duplicate, maximum-size, repeated, or out-of-order cases.
Hiding failures instead of representing loading, empty, rejected, and error states explicitly.
Optimizing before measuring the actual bottleneck or risk.
Explaining what the implementation does without explaining why its invariant proves correctness.

Is the boundary inclusive or exclusive?
Can an invalid or repeated event mutate valid state?
Are asynchronous or external results stale, missing, or out of order?
Does the representation match the operation mix and constraints?
Did the repair pass the original failure and nearby regression cases?

lessons.title: Examples, features, labels, and matrices
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Examples, features, labels, and matrices within a small, documented prediction system.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Examples, features, labels, and matrices to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Examples, features, labels, and matrices is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Represent n examples with d numeric features as an n-by-d matrix and align each supervised target with exactly one row.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Examples, features, labels, and matrices, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use vectors, matrices, distributions, functions, losses, and error costs. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Examples, features, labels, and matrices
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.name: candidate_input
variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.name: constraint_result
variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

variables_and_state.name: next_state
variables_and_state.role: A proposed state computed without corrupting current_state

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: Represent n examples with d numeric features as an n-by-d matrix and align each supervised target with exactly one row.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.
step_by_step_reasoning: Restate the problem as a testable input-output contract.
List state variables and separate current state from a candidate update.
Write constraints as predicates with visible boundary choices.
Apply the structural rule for Examples, features, labels, and matrices.
Trace the normal case one transition at a time.
Trace an exact boundary and one invalid case.
Compare observed output and preserved invariants with the contract.
Record the first divergent state if the check fails.

worked_examples.title: Normal case: contract to verified output
worked_examples.scenario: A learner applies Examples, features, labels, and matrices while building a small, documented prediction system.
worked_examples.input: One well-formed input that satisfies the documented preconditions.
reasoning: Name the observable output before choosing an operation.
Represent only the state and relationships needed for that output.
Represent n examples with d numeric features as an n-by-d matrix and align each supervised target with exactly one row.
Trace the transition and compare the result with the contract.
worked_examples.output: A valid state transition with the promised result and recorded evidence.

worked_examples.title: Boundary case: valid at the limit
worked_examples.scenario: The input is exactly at the smallest or largest documented valid boundary.
worked_examples.input: A boundary value explicitly included by the constraint.
reasoning: Write the inclusive or exclusive boundary symbolically.
Evaluate the predicate before changing state.
Apply the same rule used for ordinary valid input.
Verify that the output remains representable and accessible.
worked_examples.output: The boundary case is accepted once and produces a valid output without special hidden state.

worked_examples.title: Rejected case: preserve the invariant
worked_examples.scenario: An input violates one required relationship or arrives in an unsupported state.
worked_examples.input: An out-of-contract value paired with a previously valid state.
reasoning: Identify the failed constraint and stop before commit.
Keep the previous valid state unchanged.
Return a specific, non-sensitive explanation or recovery path.
Record the case as evidence for a regression check.
worked_examples.output: A controlled rejection, preserved prior state, and actionable feedback.

common_mistakes: Beginning implementation before defining the required output.
Changing state before the input or transition has been validated.
Memorizing the label 'Examples, features, labels, and matrices' without applying its governing relationship.
Testing only one convenient normal case and assuming boundaries behave identically.
edge_cases: The smallest valid input or empty valid structure, when allowed.
The largest documented input, count, depth, size, or duration.
A duplicate, repeated event, retry, or already-completed transition.
Malformed, missing, stale, unauthorized, or otherwise out-of-contract input.
debugging_strategy: Freeze the first input that produces a wrong observable result.
Write the expected trace beside the observed trace.
Locate the first row where state, constraint, or output diverges.
Repair the rule or boundary responsible for that first divergence.
Rerun the failing case plus one normal, one boundary, and one rejection case.
progressive_hints: Label the input and promised output before naming any tool or syntax.

lessons.title: Scaling and normalization
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Scaling and normalization within a small, documented prediction system.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Scaling and normalization to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Scaling and normalization is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Rescaling changes feature geometry and optimization behavior; fit transformation parameters only on training data.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Scaling and normalization, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.body: Use vectors, matrices, distributions, functions, losses, and error costs. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Reproducible data pipelines is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Version data, code, parameters, random seeds, and environment so the same inputs produce traceable outputs.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Reproducible data pipelines, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

project.title: Python Data and Mathematical Foundations: Responsible Machine-Learning Model Card And Prototype
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a small, documented prediction system that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate responsible machine-learning model card and prototype that demonstrates all eight skills from Python Data and Mathematical Foundations. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: Represent n examples with d numeric features as an n-by-d matrix and align each supervised target with exactly one row.
A dot product combines aligned components into a weighted sum; magnitude and angle affect how it should be interpreted.
A model is a parameterized function that maps an input vector to a prediction with a documented output meaning.
Center, spread, quantiles, and shape describe different distribution properties and can reveal outliers or skew.
Rescaling changes feature geometry and optimization behavior; fit transformation parameters only on training data.
Absence can be informative or accidental; document its mechanism, choose a treatment, and preserve an indicator when needed.
Training, validation, and test sets serve different decisions, and no future or target-derived information may cross backward.
Version data, code, parameters, random seeds, and environment so the same inputs produce traceable outputs.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Tree-based partitioning is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. A decision tree recursively partitions feature space by rules that improve target separation while risking overfit when too deep.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Tree-based partitioning, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

lessons.title: Train, fit, predict, and transform
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Train, fit, predict, and transform within a small, documented prediction system.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Train, fit, predict, and transform to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Train, fit, predict, and transform is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Fitting learns parameters from training data; prediction applies the learned mapping, while transformation changes representations.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Train, fit, predict, and transform, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use vectors, matrices, distributions, functions, losses, and error costs. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Train, fit, predict, and transform
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.name: candidate_input
variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.name: constraint_result
variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

variables_and_state.name: next_state
variables_and_state.role: A proposed state computed without corrupting current_state

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: Fitting learns parameters from training data; prediction applies the learned mapping, while transformation changes representations.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.
step_by_step_reasoning: Restate the problem as a testable input-output contract.
List state variables and separate current state from a candidate update.
Write constraints as predicates with visible boundary choices.
Apply the structural rule for Train, fit, predict, and transform.
Trace the normal case one transition at a time.
Trace an exact boundary and one invalid case.
Compare observed output and preserved invariants with the contract.
Record the first divergent state if the check fails.

project.title: Supervised and Unsupervised Learning: Responsible Machine-Learning Model Card And Prototype
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a small, documented prediction system that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate responsible machine-learning model card and prototype that demonstrates all eight skills from Supervised and Unsupervised Learning. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: Regression maps features to a continuous value and is evaluated against the size and meaning of numeric errors.
Classification estimates class evidence or probability and applies a threshold or decision rule tied to error costs.
A linear model combines features through weights and an intercept, creating an interpretable flat decision surface.
A decision tree recursively partitions feature space by rules that improve target separation while risking overfit when too deep.
Nearest-neighbor methods predict from nearby training examples under a chosen distance and scaling, with storage and query costs.
Clustering groups examples by an explicit similarity objective, but groups do not automatically equal meaningful real-world categories.
Fitting learns parameters from training data; prediction applies the learned mapping, while transformation changes representations.
A simple baseline exposes whether a model adds useful signal and which assumptions fail on important subgroups or ranges.

lessons.title: Feature engineering and valid information
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Feature engineering and valid information within a small, documented prediction system.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Feature engineering and valid information to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Feature engineering and valid information is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Create features from information available at prediction time and document their meaning, units, and failure cases.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Feature engineering and valid information, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use vectors, matrices, distributions, functions, losses, and error costs. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

content_blocks.body: Regression metrics and scale is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. MAE, squared-error measures, and relative metrics weight errors differently and must be interpreted in target units and distribution.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Regression metrics and scale, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use vectors, matrices, distributions, functions, losses, and error costs. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Regression metrics and scale
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.name: candidate_input
variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: MAE, squared-error measures, and relative metrics weight errors differently and must be interpreted in target units and distribution.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.
step_by_step_reasoning: Restate the problem as a testable input-output contract.
List state variables and separate current state from a candidate update.
Write constraints as predicates with visible boundary choices.
Apply the structural rule for Regression metrics and scale.
Trace the normal case one transition at a time.
Trace an exact boundary and one invalid case.
Compare observed output and preserved invariants with the contract.
Record the first divergent state if the check fails.

Evaluate the predicate before changing state.

reasoning: Identify the failed constraint and stop before commit.
Keep the previous valid state unchanged.
Return a specific, non-sensitive explanation or recovery path.

common_mistakes: Beginning implementation before defining the required output.
Changing state before the input or transition has been validated.
Memorizing the label 'Regression metrics and scale' without applying its governing relationship.
Testing only one convenient normal case and assuming boundaries behave identically.
edge_cases: The smallest valid input or empty valid structure, when allowed.
The largest documented input, count, depth, size, or duration.
A duplicate, repeated event, retry, or already-completed transition.
Malformed, missing, stale, unauthorized, or otherwise out-of-contract input.
debugging_strategy: Freeze the first input that produces a wrong observable result.
Write the expected trace beside the observed trace.
Locate the first row where state, constraint, or output diverges.
Repair the rule or boundary responsible for that first divergence.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Underfitting, overfitting, and regularization is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Compare training and validation behavior; regularization constrains flexibility to improve generalization rather than training fit.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Underfitting, overfitting, and regularization, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

project.title: Features, Evaluation, Bias and Model Selection: Responsible Machine-Learning Model Card And Prototype
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a small, documented prediction system that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate responsible machine-learning model card and prototype that demonstrates all eight skills from Features, Evaluation, Bias and Model Selection. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: Create features from information available at prediction time and document their meaning, units, and failure cases.
A confusion matrix counts actual-versus-predicted classes and is the source for precision, recall, specificity, and related metrics.
Changing a score threshold trades false positives against false negatives; choose it from operational costs and capacity.
MAE, squared-error measures, and relative metrics weight errors differently and must be interpreted in target units and distribution.
Use validation folds to estimate choice performance while keeping the final test set untouched until decisions are complete.
Compare training and validation behavior; regularization constrains flexibility to improve generalization rather than training fit.
Aggregate performance can hide unequal errors; evaluate meaningful groups with sample sizes and uncertainty visible.
Record hypotheses, configurations, metrics, seeds, exclusions, and negative results before drawing bounded conclusions.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Regularization and generalization is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Weight penalties, data augmentation, dropout, and early stopping constrain effective capacity in different ways.

Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

project.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning Foundations: Responsible Machine-Learning Model Card And Prototype
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a small, documented prediction system that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate responsible machine-learning model card and prototype that demonstrates all eight skills from Neural Networks and Deep Learning Foundations. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: A layer maps an input tensor shape to an output shape using learned parameters; shape compatibility is a structural invariant.
Nonlinear activations allow stacked layers to represent more than one linear transformation, while saturation affects gradients.
A loss converts prediction error into a scalar training signal and must match output meaning, data distribution, and error costs.
Backpropagation applies the chain rule through the computation graph to assign each parameter its contribution to loss change.
An optimizer updates parameters opposite the estimated gradient; step size balances slow progress against instability.
A batch estimates the full-data gradient, an epoch processes the training set, and shuffling changes correlation in updates.
Weight penalties, data augmentation, dropout, and early stopping constrain effective capacity in different ways.
Learning curves, gradient norms, data checks, and baseline comparisons distinguish optimization, representation, leakage, and overfit problems.

Treating an observed normal result as proof for every boundary.
Choosing a structure because it is familiar rather than because its operations match the constraints.

lessons.title: Data drift and performance monitoring
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Data drift and performance monitoring within a small, documented prediction system.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Data drift and performance monitoring to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Data drift and performance monitoring is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Monitor input and prediction distributions continuously, but confirm quality drift with delayed ground truth when available.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Data drift and performance monitoring, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use vectors, matrices, distributions, functions, losses, and error costs. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Data drift and performance monitoring
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract

lessons.title: Fairness, privacy, and human oversight
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Fairness, privacy, and human oversight within a small, documented prediction system.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Fairness, privacy, and human oversight to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Fairness, privacy, and human oversight is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Evaluate affected groups, minimize data, protect sensitive attributes, define appeal, and assign humans meaningful decision authority.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Fairness, privacy, and human oversight, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use vectors, matrices, distributions, functions, losses, and error costs. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Fairness, privacy, and human oversight
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.name: candidate_input
variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.name: constraint_result
variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

variables_and_state.name: next_state
variables_and_state.role: A proposed state computed without corrupting current_state

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: Evaluate affected groups, minimize data, protect sensitive attributes, define appeal, and assign humans meaningful decision authority.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.
step_by_step_reasoning: Restate the problem as a testable input-output contract.
List state variables and separate current state from a candidate update.
Write constraints as predicates with visible boundary choices.
Apply the structural rule for Fairness, privacy, and human oversight.
Trace the normal case one transition at a time.
Trace an exact boundary and one invalid case.
Compare observed output and preserved invariants with the contract.
Record the first divergent state if the check fails.

worked_examples.scenario: A learner applies Fairness, privacy, and human oversight while building a small, documented prediction system.
worked_examples.input: One well-formed input that satisfies the documented preconditions.
reasoning: Name the observable output before choosing an operation.
Represent only the state and relationships needed for that output.
Evaluate affected groups, minimize data, protect sensitive attributes, define appeal, and assign humans meaningful decision authority.
Trace the transition and compare the result with the contract.
worked_examples.output: A valid state transition with the promised result and recorded evidence.

worked_examples.title: Boundary case: valid at the limit
worked_examples.scenario: The input is exactly at the smallest or largest documented valid boundary.
worked_examples.input: A boundary value explicitly included by the constraint.
reasoning: Write the inclusive or exclusive boundary symbolically.
Evaluate the predicate before changing state.
Apply the same rule used for ordinary valid input.
Verify that the output remains representable and accessible.
worked_examples.output: The boundary case is accepted once and produces a valid output without special hidden state.

worked_examples.title: Rejected case: preserve the invariant
worked_examples.scenario: An input violates one required relationship or arrives in an unsupported state.
worked_examples.input: An out-of-contract value paired with a previously valid state.
reasoning: Identify the failed constraint and stop before commit.
Keep the previous valid state unchanged.
Return a specific, non-sensitive explanation or recovery path.
Record the case as evidence for a regression check.
worked_examples.output: A controlled rejection, preserved prior state, and actionable feedback.

structured_representation.caption: A validate-before-commit trace for Fairness, privacy, and human oversight.

common_mistakes: Beginning implementation before defining the required output.
Changing state before the input or transition has been validated.
Memorizing the label 'Fairness, privacy, and human oversight' without applying its governing relationship.
Testing only one convenient normal case and assuming boundaries behave identically.
edge_cases: The smallest valid input or empty valid structure, when allowed.
The largest documented input, count, depth, size, or duration.
A duplicate, repeated event, retry, or already-completed transition.
Malformed, missing, stale, unauthorized, or otherwise out-of-contract input.
debugging_strategy: Freeze the first input that produces a wrong observable result.
Write the expected trace beside the observed trace.
Locate the first row where state, constraint, or output diverges.
Repair the rule or boundary responsible for that first divergence.
Rerun the failing case plus one normal, one boundary, and one rejection case.

Apply this rule, then trace the boundary: Evaluate affected groups, minimize data, protect sensitive attributes, define appeal, and assign humans meaningful decision authority.

project.title: Production ML, Monitoring and Responsible AI: Responsible Machine-Learning Model Card And Prototype
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a small, documented prediction system that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate responsible machine-learning model card and prototype that demonstrates all eight skills from Production ML, Monitoring and Responsible AI. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: Production preprocessing and feature definitions must match training exactly or predictions operate on a different input space.
A deployable model specifies version, feature schema, output semantics, latency, resource limits, and failure behavior.
Monitor input and prediction distributions continuously, but confirm quality drift with delayed ground truth when available.
Model decisions can change future data; evaluation must account for selection effects, missing outcomes, and label delay.
Shadow, canary, or staged deployment limits exposure while predefined metrics and rollback criteria control risk.
Evaluate affected groups, minimize data, protect sensitive attributes, define appeal, and assign humans meaningful decision authority.
Document purpose, data, metrics, limitations, ethical considerations, owners, and prohibited uses for accountable deployment.
Detect harmful behavior, contain model or data changes, preserve evidence, restore a safe baseline, and update controls from lessons learned.

starter_materials.scaffold_policy: Level 5 supplies only constraints, acceptance criteria, and review checkpoints.

mandatory_features: Demonstrate Training-serving consistency and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Model packaging and inference contracts and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Data drift and performance monitoring and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Feedback loops and delayed labels and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Safe rollout and rollback and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Fairness, privacy, and human oversight and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Model cards and decision documentation and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Incident response for ML systems and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
constraints: Use only the languages, components, or structural interactions supported by the target application environment.
Do not hide invalid input, unavailable data, or failure behind a successful-looking state.
Keep current valid state recoverable until a candidate transition passes validation.
Do not embed secrets, real credentials, personal data, or private endpoints.
Make all important output and error states accessible and testable.
Record assumptions and unsupported cases explicitly.
The submitted result must be reproducible from the included instructions.

test_cases.expected: one correct output and valid next state

test_cases.condition: second valid input with different data

test_cases.expected: accepted only if contract includes it

test_cases.condition: valid retry after a controlled failure

edge_cases: empty or minimum
maximum documented size
duplicate or retry
out-of-order or stale result
malformed or unauthorized input
debugging_checklist: Freeze a reproducible failing input.
Compare expected and observed traces.
Find the first divergent state.
Check the constraint at that transition.
Repair cause before symptoms.
Rerun the failure and adjacent cases.
Confirm state recovery and accessible feedback.
Record the limitation if the case remains unsupported.
completion_checklist: All eight level skills appear in the artifact or evidence.
The input-output contract is complete.
The structural model matches the implementation or decision flow.
All eight required test categories have evidence.
The rubric self-score totals 100 possible points.
No secret, real credential, or sensitive personal data is included.
Submission instructions reproduce the result.
Reflection names one failure, repair, and justified improvement.
submission_requirements: README with setup or review instructions

rubric.evidence: inputs, outputs, constraints, diagram, and milestones
mandatory behavior matches the project contract
clear responsibilities, transitions, and dependency boundaries
normal, boundary, invalid, repeated, and failure cases
usable states, safe handling, and recovery feedback
setup, decisions, limitations, evidence, and reproducible instructions
first divergence, repair, trade-off, and next iteration

common_failure_conditions: The result handles only one normal case.
State changes before validation.
A level skill is named but not demonstrated.
The diagram disagrees with the implemented flow.
A failed dependency leaves a false success state.
Submission evidence cannot be reproduced.
reflection_questions: Which assumption changed after the first trace?
Where did expected and observed state first diverge?
Which invariant prevented the most serious failure?
What trade-off did you make among clarity, cost, performance, accessibility, safety, or flexibility?
What evidence would you collect before a wider release?
optional_extensions: Add a second representation and compare which relationships become easier to inspect.
Add property-based or generated boundary cases without duplicating existing tests.
Measure one performance, quality, or risk indicator and justify an improvement threshold.
Design a migration or compatibility plan for one changed requirement.
project.acceptable_outcome_example: A submission may use the supplied contract and state templates, implement one complete primary journey, show all required failure states, and provide eight passing test records plus one documented limitation. The exact implementation remains the learner's work.

prompts.prompt: Restate the final input-output contract in one sentence.
Describe the first state where expected and observed behavior diverged.
Explain the repair and the invariant or constraint it restored.
Name one design trade-off and the evidence behind your choice.
What is the safest and most valuable next improvement?

optional_mastery_challenge.title: Optional Mastery Transfer
optional_mastery_challenge.prompt: Transfer the level's eight governing rules to a new version of a small, documented prediction system with one changed constraint, one new failure state, and one stricter evidence requirement.
required_outputs: change-impact table across all eight skills
normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery traces
success_criteria: The changed constraint is applied consistently.
No unaffected invariant is silently removed.
The new failure state has visible recovery behavior.
Evidence distinguishes old and new behavior.
